headline: Oil sinks ~6-7% on eve of US midterms as dialogue signals rise
dek: Oil prices sank around 6-7% on Monday, the eve of the US midterm elections, as signals that Tehran and Washington are renewing dialogue boosted hopes of ending the war: Brent down 6.1% to $106.54 (AFP via Dawn 07:17pm PKT entry) / down 6% to $106.60 (Geo.tv), WTI down 6.3-6.4% to $97.49-97.56.…
sources: AFP (via Dawn liveblog); Geo.tv; Axios (letter, via AFP)
fault_line: Is the oil-price drop a real peace signal, or a tactical pre-election feint while Hormuz attacks continue?

sections.what_happened: Oil prices sank around 6-7% on Monday, the eve of the US midterm elections, as signals that Tehran and Washington are renewing dialogue boosted hopes of ending the war: Brent down 6.1% to $106.54 (AFP via Dawn 07:17pm PKT entry) / down 6% to $106.60 (Geo.tv), WTI down 6.3-6.4% to $97.49-97.56. Axios reported US Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian national security chief Mohsen Rezaei about possible new talks -- described by AFP as the highest-level Trump-administration move in months. Analyst Arne Lohmann Rasmussen (Global Risk Management) cautioned: 'We believe the (Trump) signals may be tactical ahead of tomorrow's US midterm elections,' noting Hormuz shipping attacks continue and his firm maintains a higher-for-longer energy-price outlook. This updates (not repeats) the mid-day prints recorded earlier today (Brent -4.2% to $108.64 at 1020 GMT; WTI -4.1% to $99.83). The Vance letter had not previously been recorded as a standalone item in today's scans.
sections.what_verified: Two distinct publisher families for the price move: AFP (T1 wire) and Geo News (T3). The Vance letter rests on Axios reporting relayed by AFP -- one family for that element.
sections.what_disputed: The price fall is a sentiment move, not a settlement: Hormuz attacks continued through the day (UKMTO projectile strike east of Ras Al-Khafji; Iranian Navy mine claim east of Hormuz, both already recorded), and the analyst quote itself warns the signals may be tactical pre-election positioning. No US or Iranian confirmation of the Vance letter's contents has been published, and no agreement text exists -- the Doha draft proposal reported earlier today remains unattributed to any published document.
sections.why_matters: Oil just fell 7% on talk of peace -- on the eve of the vote that decides whether Trump can afford war. The pocketbook signal vs the Hormuz reality: attacks continued today. Diplomacy, or a pause priced for the midterms?
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (Dawn liveblog 11:07pm PKT = 22:07 , AFP; Geo.tv corroboration) -- Oil sinks ~6-7% on eve of US midterms as dialogue signals rise; Axios reports Vance letter to Rezaei
